script.base: Closing TEN -1.5 with a 39.5 total (implied TEN 20.5, NYJ 19.0) is a pick'em slog outdoors, not a shootout and not a blowout. Both sides lean run; the leader, if either pulls ahead late, clocks it with the lead back. Pace stays modest, so pass-yard monsters are the numbers that need a script flip.
script.flip1: NYJ scores first and leads, TEN abandons the run, Pollard's rush line dies, and Ayomanor/Robinson/Dike plus a chasing Cam-less volume bump (no 2026 QB named in the pack) become the pass game. Hall's carries stall the same way.
script.flip2: TEN gets up by two scores, runs Pollard/Carter late, and NYJ throws short and often. Wilson/Mitchell/Taylor volume rises while TEN WR overs stall. Unsaved wind or rain would drag both pass games and the total under.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both leans lost. Pollard under 60.5 because this was a committee: Carter took the series the 60.5 line was trying to fade, the Jets' front stuffed the run even without Ossai, and NYJ led so Tennessee threw. The 104/102/85 were a different 2025 offense and did not travel. Taylor under 21.5 because the backup linebacker was fine, the Jets lived in a 19-point run game behind Hall, and Taylor's 2025 target share belonged to another quarterback — the two 21-yard games were the real role, and 21.5 needed one more catch that never came. Unsaved wind or rain would have made the pass miss even if Gray's replacement was bad.
slip_story: One low-total competitive story, not a shootout stack: TEN clocks with the lead back (Pollard rush over) and NYJ's limited pass game is the short hook to the TE because Gray is out (Taylor rec over). They can win together in a 20-17 type game. They are not opposite scripts, but they are not a forced correlation either — a pure Jets run game hits Pollard and misses Taylor. No TD legs, one market per player, two legs only because no third name cleared the read. Wilson under 71.5 was considered (last4 median well under 71.5 in a 19-point team total) and dropped: Patrick Out is a stronger counter than the under, and a 1.5-point game can flip NYJ into a chase.
